input.prompt: Use the reference image as the style and craft reference: paint a NEW panel that is a sibling of it, with exactly the same lotus-and-vine border around all four edges (lotus-and-vine scroll between two thin dotted bands on ecru), the same deep madder red ground, the same dye palette, the same iron-black kalam line quality, the same dense dot, cross-hatch and scale fill patterns, and the same visible hand-woven cotton texture. This must look like a real old Srikalahasti kalamkari temple cloth painted by hand with a bamboo kalam, not a modern digital illustration and not a comic: lines are hand-drawn, slightly wobbly, of varying thickness, with small dye bleed; every garment and object is filled with dense hand-drawn patterns of dots, tiny flowers, stripes, scales and cross-hatching; each figure is surrounded by a thin dotted ecru outline; small scattered lotus buds, dots and tiny flower sprigs decorate the empty red ground between the figures, as in the reference. Photographed flat and straight-on so the cloth fills the entire frame edge to edge. Subject: a Telugu engagement ceremony (nischitartham). Across the top, a flat patterned canopy (pandal) whose edge is hung with a festoon garland of mango leaves and marigold flowers. Below it stand exactly six people in one row, full figures from head to feet, drawn in the classical kalamkari figure style: faces in strict side profile with one large elongated almond eye, long curved eyebrow, pointed nose, stylised hands with long curling fingers, patterned drapery with zig-zag pleats. At the centre the young couple face each other: on the left the young man (short black hair, neat short black beard, round glasses, a plain forehead with no mark, a cream kurta patterned with tiny dots and white pyjama), on the right the young woman (long black braid with white jasmine flowers, a madder red silk saree with an indigo and yellow patterned border). BOTH of them are holding a ring: the young man holds a small yellow ring between thumb and finger toward her, and the young woman holds her own small yellow ring between thumb and finger toward him; their hands are close but not touching; each of them uses only one hand for the ring and the other arm hangs relaxed at the side. On the far left stand the young man's parents side by side, on the far right stand the young woman's parents side by side; in each pair an older man of about sixty with grey-white hair and a grey moustache, in a white dhoti with an angavastram, and an older woman of about fifty-five with grey streaked hair in a bun with jasmine, in a patterned saree; the parents must clearly look a generation older than the couple. Each of the four elders holds his or her own separate round plate of thambulam in both hands, four plates in total, each plate heaped with green betel leaves, yellow bananas, a brown coconut, flowers, and a folded silk saree. At the bottom, a band of small lotus flowers and leaves on the ground line. Palette: flat natural vegetable-dye fills only: deep madder red (alizarin, brick red), indigo blue, myrobalan-turmeric yellow, green made from indigo over yellow, and undyed ecru cotton; skin of all figures is flat ecru-ochre. Every person has two arms, two hands with five fingers, and one face. Completely flat, no perspective, no shading, no gradients, no metallic gold, no 3D, no photorealism. No text, no letters, no writing, no script, no numbers, no inscriptions. No lamps, no diyas, no oil lamps, no candles, no fire, no flames anywhere.
